title: Amazing Grace (arranged for beginners)
subtitle: Hymn tune "New Britain", simple two-hand setting in 3/4
trains: A well-known pentatonic melody with a one-beat pickup, in half, quarter and a few eighth notes, over a single sustained bass note per bar - gentle two-hand reading at a slow tempo.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: The hymn tune "New Britain" (the "Amazing Grace" tune; Virginia Harmony, 1831) in the form harmonized by E. O. Excell (1900), both public domain. The melody is the Soprano of the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond engraving (piece-info id 1283, new_britain.ly, typeset by Steve Dunlop from www.cyberhymnal.org); the audit record content/library/audit/repertoire/beginner/amazing-grace.json re-checks it note by note.
provenance.note: A one-beat pickup and 15 bars in G major at quarter = 72. The right hand plays the tune exactly as the source gives it, rhythm included; the left hand holds one bass note per bar.

departures: Left hand: our own setting, one held note per bar from E. O. Excell's bass, not his four-part harmony; where his bass moves, the longer note is kept (bars 9, 11, 12), C in bar 10, D in bar 14.
